abstract: The Immune Epitope Database (IEDB, iedb.org) is a freely available resource cataloging experimentally defined immune epitopes and, where reported, the immune receptors that recognize them. The IEDB currently records ∼235 000 distinct T cell receptors and ∼6400 distinct B cell receptors/antibodies with experimentally verified epitope specificity. Here, we describe recent updates to the IEDB, centered on a comprehensive revision of these receptor data. Because receptors were curated from 3879 references spanning decades, heterogeneity in gene nomenclature and CDR delimitation presents challenges for computational analyses and user queries. We rebuilt the standardization and validation pipeline to compute IUIS/IMGT-compliant V/D/J gene names and consistently delimited V domain, CDR1, 2, 3, and Junction sequences, and identify anomalous receptors from 822 references for re-curation. The IEDB web interface was expanded to include receptor search features directly on the homepage, support V/J gene and species options in the refined receptor search, and direct data export in the Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire (AIRR) format. We anticipate that the improved data quality will simplify bioinformatics analyses and facilitate integration into cross-repository data resources, such as the AIRR Knowledge Commons.
